questions_and_answers.question_text: What three things may follow the verb shì when identifying someone?

answers.answer_text: The full name alone, the surname plus title, or the full name plus title.

questions_and_answers.question_text: What is the literal meaning of Xiānsheng?
How does the connotation of Xiānsheng compare with that of the English "Mr."?

answers.answer_text: Xiānsheng has more of a connotation of respectfulness than "Mr." does.

questions_and_answers.question_text: To whom is the title Xiānsheng usually applied?
Why should you not say Wǒ shi Jones Xiānsheng, and what should you say instead?

answers.answer_text: Respectful titles such as Xiānsheng are not used when giving your own name; you say Wǒ xìng Jones instead.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Give another example of a respectful title mentioned in the notes, together with its meaning.
When a name and a title are said together, which part receives the heavy stress?

answers.answer_text: The name receives the heavy stress, as in WÁNG Xiānsheng.

questions_and_answers.question_text: How is the title often pronounced when it follows a name in rapid speech?
Write the Chinese sentence meaning "He is Mr. Mǎ Mínglǐ."
Using the pattern in the table, write a Chinese sentence identifying someone by surname plus title only.

articles.text:
7. A: Tā shi shéi?                          Who is he?
   B: Tā shi Mǎ Xiānsheng.                  He is Mr. Mǎ.

8. A: Tā shi shéi?                          Who is he?
   B: Tā shi Mǎ Mínglǐ Xiānsheng.           He is Mr. Mǎ Mínglǐ.

Notes on Nos. 7-8

After the verb shì you may have the full name alone, the surname plus title, or the full name plus title.

| Tā | shi | Mǎ | Mínglǐ. |            |
| Tā | shi | Mǎ |         | Xiānsheng. |
| Tā | shi | Mǎ | Mínglǐ  | Xiānsheng. |

Xiānsheng, literally "first-born," has more of a connotation of respectfulness than "Mr." Xiānsheng is usually applied only to people other than oneself. Do not use the title Xiānsheng (or any other respectful title, such as Jiàoshòu, "Professor") when giving your own name. If you want to say "I am Mr. Jones," you may say Wǒ xìng Jones.

When a name and title are said together, logically enough it is the name which gets the heavy stress: WÁNG Xiānsheng. You will often hear the title pronounced with no full tones: WÁNG Xiansheng.
